feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across skills sections, and could sharpen impact by quantifying more outcomes beyond scope/activity.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary establish a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and public-sector communications.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions within one organization support leadership growth and reliability.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a tighter structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-based metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities (“led,” “supported,” “advised”) without showing business/user results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, or cost savings.  
- Fix minor style consistency issues: use parallel punctuation in lists (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. elsewhere without the serial comma), standardize date formatting, and consider replacing “Ranked among the top public universities…” since it adds little value. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads a bit broad and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale or outcomes.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like structure; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a scale cue from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast “Leads” to “Leads/has led” or make the whole summary third-person-free for consistency.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance, and content operations. Has led enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search and content experiences.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is echoed repeatedly elsewhere; avoid stacking all three unless adding specificity.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership areas rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper competency labels and keep parallel structure throughout.
- Prioritize the most marketable and recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia leadership.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “website” with “web” and “content experiences” with “content discovery” for cleaner, more specific phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” repeats positioning already established in the header and multiple roles.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps with Topline Skills and several NACo experience bullets.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot that reinforces the headline well, but it reads a bit dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects:” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and cleaner lists: “combined hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Where available, add scope or outcome signals (audience, campaign purpose, platform, or business value) to make projects feel less generic.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series closely repeat achievements already covered in recent roles.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing projects not already described in work experience.

items.title: Coleman Davis

items.content: Senior digital leader with more than 12 years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your NACo leadership bullets. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, scope, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded full-time consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal-based campaign experiences, and enterprise web improvement.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Redesigned cross-functional content workflows, governance, and analytics to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Built modular Drupal microsites, campaign pages, and member toolkits; delivered front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Keep the AI work as the differentiator: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if possible (adoption, search success, time saved, pages/templates launched).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “analytics” repeat language from NACo; use consulting-specific outcomes instead.
- “Large public-facing web properties” is vague—quantify or cut.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in the earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, open/click rates, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Combine infrastructure/governance points: “Built analytics and publishing systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and measurable scale.
- Video/studio language may echo earlier NACo multimedia bullets; emphasize building institutional capacity, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems-building before the higher-level strategy/patform work in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet for outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” since the Director role already uses nearly identical channel-language.
- “Strengthened workflows/governance” also appears in both adjacent NACo roles; keep this version focused on day-to-day execution, not governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctiveness rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & UX
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “content operations” or “digital transformation” to better reflect recent leadership work.
- Add one more specific capability if space allows, such as “stakeholder alignment” or “platform modernization,” both well supported by recent roles.
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid softer phrases like “audience-focused” when “audience strategy” is more senior and concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already strongly established in the summary and NACo experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a platform inventory to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-sounding items like “jQuery” unless it is required for target roles.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for large public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” is already repeated in Technical + IT; avoid listing the same tools in both sections.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with the Automation & Workflow Systems section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for your most recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around decision-making impact and avoid repeating “reporting/analytics” language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome, e.g.:
- GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI
- KPI framework design and executive dashboarding
- Performance analysis, user behavior insights, and optimization
- SEO and content performance measurement
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure and decision support” or “measurement for enterprise web and campaign performance.”
- Keep the strongest, most current tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- This overlaps with the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure, so keep this section concise and capability-focused, not narrative.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to current/recent strengths and tools, not broad production jargon.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio & Live Event Delivery
- Tighten and modernize the list: Video production & editing • Livestream production • PTZ camera operation • Broadcast studio operations • Hybrid/virtual event delivery
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability tied to recent work: Executive/advocacy video production or Broadcast-quality in-house studio production
- Consider replacing “Livestreaming” with “Livestream production” and “PTZ camera systems” with “PTZ camera operation” for stronger, action-oriented phrasing

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; keep this version more technical/tactical.
- Avoid repeating “studio” or “event production” language already covered in the Director of Digital Media role unless this section adds tool/process specificity.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize platform administration/publishing systems or reduced to avoid repeating the same tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web CMS Administration
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent relevance: Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it reflects meaningful professional use; it reads lighter than the enterprise platforms above

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; keep the richer version in one place and make this one shorter
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid adding extra descriptors here that repeat the work experience bullets

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical mix, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize current, hands-on tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, execution-oriented list: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Serverless/dev workflow: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in parentheses for stronger credibility, e.g., “API integrations (CMS, analytics, member tools)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment automation).”
- Order by current relevance/impact: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under analytics/optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Since workflow architecture is already a core theme elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly grouped.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not as one flat list: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with your recent consulting and digital operations work.
- Put the strongest/most relevant tools first based on recent use and differentiation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one brief proof point tied to recent roles, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Microsoft tools.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them last or remove if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare compared with the rest of the CV. Since email is a recurring strength in recent roles, this line should signal level of use or scope, not just list tools.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience engagement)
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: “admin/configuration,” “template management,” or “segmentation and sends.”
- Keep naming consistent and concise; consider shortening to “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights” if “Journeys” is implied by your use.
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and relevance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with multiple work bullets about leading email newsletters; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you remove them from experience.
- “Engagement Systems” may overstate scope if these were mainly email platforms; “Email Platforms” would be tighter.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set for recent leadership roles, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more specific to analysis/optimization methods or trim it to avoid repeating the same platforms twice.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Analytics & Optimization Tools”
- Tighten to: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • KPI reporting • Conversion analysis”
- Replace vague terms like “Dashboarding” with stronger, outcome-oriented language such as “KPI reporting” or “executive dashboards”
- Only keep “A/B testing” if you can support it with real examples; otherwise swap for “behavior analysis” or “performance measurement”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping platforms here and reserving methods/outcomes for the Topline section
- “SEO” also risks overlap with broader digital strategy language unless supported elsewhere in experience bullets

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and distinct as the early build phase of the digital function.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, establishing workflows across web, email, social media and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video content; coordinated day-to-day digital publishing and multimedia delivery.”
- Tighten the management reference: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume, audience growth, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep that later role focused on scaling the channel, and this one on launching/producing it.
- “Strengthening workflows” also appears in later NACo roles; here, frame it as building initial processes rather than improving mature operations.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation for later digital/media leadership, with more emphasis on outcomes and less on broad support work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest achievement first: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with a clearer scope: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for county-facing programs and policy teams.”
- Add any measurable outcomes if available: number of episodes, audience/listens, internal stakeholders supported, or multimedia assets produced.
- Consider a tighter version: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams while contributing digital and multimedia content. Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on the podcast and program/policy support.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/media leadership here since stronger, more recent examples appear in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful skills, but this item is too generic and repeats stronger claims already made in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize software/tools only, with production capabilities shown in recent experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Creative Software & Production Tools
- Replace with: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want one capability phrase, keep it concise: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing
- Move any broader phrasing like “livestream studio workflows” out of this tools list unless you add specific platforms/equipment.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”) and Topline Skills (“Livestreaming,” “Studio operations”).
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older experience; if retained here, consider “Podcast editing” to keep this section tool-focused.
